headline: ROGUE's floor is now a minefield
lede: The never-dry picker sent slot a to Rogue's oldest honest gap — no traps at all — and the 1980 minefield moved in: hidden traps on every level, an escalating trap-door fall grudge, and the teleport trap that keeps firing. Existing dungeons replay byte-identical until you step wrong.

notes.text: Seven cart kinds spring underfoot: trap door (nth consecutive fall costs (n−1)·2d6 — walk the stairs to settle the grudge), teleport (stays armed), sleep and snare (your turns burn while monsters close in), lose-strength, confusion, darts.

roguecheck 150/0 with 27 new gates; two mutants proven mortal (rng-rewind drop kills the stream anchor, a disarmed spring kills 15). roguedrive 25/25 real keys — the pinned seed's arrow-salvage run now springs a sleep mine and hauls the quiver home anyway.

Two games merged between the slots: INVADERS' machine-step march (slot b, #3578) and ROGUE's trap floor (slot a, #3581). Slot b closed its session clean; the queue is empty and never-dry resumes next tick.

Trap generation borrows and rewinds the rng slice — every pre-existing seed's dungeon, items and later levels replay byte-identical until a trap actually springs; a golden anchor gate pins seed 777 to keep it that way.
